section_1.title: The Counter-Intuitive Challenge
section_1.content: Introduce the core question: Between two points at different heights, what path allows an object to slide from start to finish in the shortest time? Contrast the 'shortest distance' (straight line) with the 'quickest time'.
section_1.example: An animation of two penguins, Pip and Pop. Pip slides down a straight icy ramp, while Pop slides down a curved ramp. Despite the longer path, Pop reaches the bottom first, sparking the 'Why?'

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Speed and Energy
section_2.content: Review the Conservation of Energy. Establish that speed (v) depends only on the vertical drop (y), represented by the formula v = √(2gy). Explain that while a curve is longer, its steeper start provides higher initial velocity.
section_2.example: A side-view graph showing a marble at various heights. As the height (y) decreases, a velocity vector arrow grows longer, visually linking height loss to speed gain.

section_3.title: The Optical Analogy (Snell's Law)
section_3.content: Introduce Bernoulli's brilliant insight: Treat the falling object like a beam of light passing through layers of varying density. Use Snell's Law (sinθ/v = constant) to explain how light 'chooses' the path of least time.
section_3.example: A visual of a lifeguard on a beach. To reach a drowning swimmer fastest, they don't run in a straight line; they run further on land (where they are fast) and less in water (where they are slow). This 'bending' is the key to the Brachistochrone.

section_4.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
section_4.content: Reveal the Brachistochrone curve as an 'Inverted Cycloid'. Define a cycloid as the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling wheel. Show the parametric relationship where the curve's curvature perfectly balances speed and distance.
section_4.example: An animation of a bicycle wheel rolling along a ceiling. A glowing red dot on the tire's edge traces a graceful arc—this is the exact shape the slide must be.

section_5.title: Properties and Verification
section_5.content: Highlight the 'Tautochrone' property: No matter where you start on the cycloid, you will reach the bottom in the exact same amount of time. Summarize the trade-off between acceleration and path length.
section_5.example: A 'Multi-Ball Race' animation. Three balls are placed at different heights on the same cycloid ramp. They are released simultaneously and all collide at the bottom at the exact same moment.

section_6.title: Real-World Application & Summary
section_6.content: Recap the journey from intuition to the cycloid. Briefly mention applications in engineering, such as the design of efficient roller coasters or gravity-based transit systems.
section_6.example: A montage of modern skatepark bowls and high-speed roller coaster loops, overlaid with the cycloid geometry to show how designers use these principles to maximize thrill and speed.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Lecture lines for Section 5
        lines = [
            "The cycloid also possesses the remarkable Tautochrone property.",
            "Objects released from any height reach the bottom simultaneously.",
            "Higher starting points cover more distance but move faster.",
            "These factors perfectly cancel out to keep time constant.",
            "This consistency confirms the cycloid's mathematical perfection."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Properties and Verification", lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid point calculation
        # x = r(theta + sin(theta)), y = r(1 - cos(theta))
        # theta in [-PI, 0] for a slide starting high on left and ending low at 0
        r_val = 0.7
        def get_cycloid_point(theta):
            return np.array([r_val * (theta + np.sin(theta)), r_val * (1 - np.cos(theta)), 0])

        # Create Ramp
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(
            get_cycloid_point,
            t_range=[-PI, 0],
            color="#C0C0C0"
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_path, "B1", "F6")
        # Store original center to position balls relative to it
        path_center = cycloid_path.get_center()
        # Adjust curve so the bottom (0,0 in parametric) is at the bottom of the area
        # The parametric (0,0) is at the right end of the path.
        # We'll just use the path as is and align relative to it.
        self.play(Create(cycloid_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Define starting thetas for three balls
        thetas_start = [-0.9 * PI, -0.6 * PI, -0.3 * PI]
        colors = ["#FF00FF", "#00FF00", "#00FFFF"]
        balls = VGroup()
        for col in colors:
            ball = Dot(radius=0.1, color=col)
            balls.add(ball)

        # Initial positioning of balls
        for i, theta in enumerate(thetas_start):
            balls[i].move_to(cycloid_path.point_from_proportion((theta + PI) / PI))

        self.play(FadeIn(balls))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Time tracker for the harmonic motion
        # Theta(t) = Theta_0 * cos(sqrt(g/4r) * t)
        # We'll normalize t so that at t=1, all reach theta=0.
        # T = (PI/2) / sqrt(g/4r)
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        def update_ball(ball, theta_0):
            # Harmonic motion towards the bottom (theta=0)
            # t goes from 0 to 1
            # Current theta = theta_0 * cos(PI/2 * time)
            t_curr = time_tracker.get_value()
            current_theta = theta_0 * np.cos((PI / 2) * t_curr)
            # Map theta to proportion [0, 1] on the path [-PI, 0]
            # proportion = (theta - (-PI)) / (0 - (-PI)) = (theta + PI) / PI
            prop = (current_theta + PI) / PI
            ball.move_to(cycloid_path.point_from_proportion(prop))

        # Add updaters
        for i in range(len(balls)):
            balls[i].add_updater(lambda b, i=i: update_ball(b, thetas_start[i]))

        # Start motion
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Balls are all at the bottom now. Add a small highlight or flash
        arrival_flash = Flash(cycloid_path.get_end(), color=WHITE, flash_radius=0.5)
        self.play(arrival_flash)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Clear updaters for static end
        for b in balls:
            b.clear_updaters()
            
        self.wait(3)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        formula = MathTex(r"v = \sqrt{2gy}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A3', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#ADFF2F")

            curr_pos = start_pt + DOWN * curr_y
            v_len = np.sqrt(curr_y) * 0.8

            t_range=[0, PI/4], # The steep initial part
            color="#FFFF00",
            stroke_width=6
        )

        self.place_in_area(viz_group, 'C3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(Create(curve))

    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Counter-Intuitive Challenge"
        lecture_lines = [
            "What path is the fastest between two points?",
            "A straight line is the shortest distance, not time.",
            "Curved paths often allow objects to reach destinations sooner."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_A = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_B = "#00BFFF"
        COLOR_STRAIGHT = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_CURVE = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_FLASH = "#FFFF00"

        # 1. Define Points A and B
        dot_a = Dot(color=COLOR_A)
        dot_b = Dot(color=COLOR_B)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_A)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_B)
        
        self.place_at_grid(dot_a, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_b, "E5")
        label_a.next_to(dot_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_b.next_to(dot_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # 2. Define Paths
        start_pos = self.grid["B2"]
        end_pos = self.grid["E5"]
        
        straight_path = Line(start_pos, end_pos, color=COLOR_STRAIGHT)
        
        # Curve: Quadratic Bezier to simulate a faster descent curve
        # Control point at E2 (drop fast then move right)
        control_pos = self.grid["E2"]
        curved_path = QuadraticBezier(start_pos, control_pos, end_pos, color=COLOR_CURVE)

        # 3. Define Sliders Pip and Pop
        pip = Dot(color=COLOR_STRAIGHT).scale(1.2)
        pip_label = Text("Pip", font_size=18, color=COLOR_STRAIGHT)
        
        pop = Dot(color=COLOR_CURVE).scale(1.2)
        pop_label = Text("Pop", font_size=18, color=COLOR_CURVE)

        # Trackers for movement
        pip_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        pop_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Updaters for position
        pip.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(straight_path.point_from_proportion(pip_tracker.get_value())))
        pip_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(pip, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        pop.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(curved_path.point_from_proportion(pop_tracker.get_value())))
        pop_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(pop, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "What path is the fastest between two points?"
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_a), FadeIn(label_a),
            FadeIn(dot_b), FadeIn(label_b),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "A straight line is the shortest distance, not time."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_STRAIGHT)
        )
        self.play(Create(straight_path), run_time=1)
        self.add(pip, pip_label)
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate.set_value(0.3), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Curved paths often allow objects to reach destinations sooner."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        )
        self.play(Create(curved_path), run_time=1)
        self.add(pop, pop_label)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Race Sequence
        # Reset Pip
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Execution of the race: Pop finishes in 2s, Pip still halfway
        self.play(
            pip_tracker.animate(rate_func=linear).set_value(0.6),
            pop_tracker.animate(rate_func=ease_in_quad).set_value(1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Pop reaches B first; curved path flashes yellow
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_FLASH), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_FLASH), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE), run_time=0.2)
        
        # Pip finishes
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate(rate_func=linear).set_value(1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#ADFF2F")
        
        start_pt = self.grid['C1']
        end_pt = self.grid['F1']
        
        marble = Dot(point=start_pt, color="#ADFF2F", radius=0.12)
        y_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Arrow function for dynamic updating
        def get_arrow():
            curr_y = y_tracker.get_value()
            curr_pos = start_pt + DOWN * curr_y
            v_len = np.sqrt(curr_y) * 0.8
            if v_len < 0.05:
                return Line(curr_pos, curr_pos, stroke_width=0)
            return Arrow(curr_pos, curr_pos + DOWN * v_len, buff=0, color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4)

        marble.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(start_pt + DOWN * y_tracker.get_value()))

        self.play(y_tracker.animate.set_value(3), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)

        marble.clear_updaters()
        self.remove(velocity_vector)
        self.add(frozen_vector)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlighting Line 3 with yellow
        
        # Cycloid Parametric: x = t - sin(t), y = -(1 - cos(t))

            lambda t: np.array([t - np.sin(t), -(1 - np.cos(t)), 0]),

        )
        
        # Grouping ensures they share the same transform from place_in_area

        self.place_in_area(viz_group, 'C3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Draw the curve, then the highlight
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(highlight_segment))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The Optical Analogy (Snell's Law)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Johann Bernoulli used an optical analogy to solve it.",
            "Imagine light traveling through layers with changing refractive indices.",
            "Snell’s Law states sin theta over velocity remains constant.",
            "Light always chooses the path of least time.",
            "This bending light path reveals the optimal physical curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lines
        colors = ["#87CEEB", "#98FB98", "#F0E68C", "#FFA07A", "#DDA0DD"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        
        # Layers of varying density
        # Representing media where light speed changes
        layer_colors = ["#003366", "#004080", "#004d99", "#0059b3", "#0066cc", "#0073e6"]
        layers = VGroup()
        for i in range(6):
            row_char = chr(65 + i)
            rect = Rectangle(width=6.0, height=1.0, fill_color=layer_colors[i], fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0.5, stroke_color=BLUE_E)
            self.place_in_area(rect, f"{row_char}1", f"{row_char}6")
            layers.add(rect)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(layers))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        
        # Bending light path (Piecewise linear segments)
        path_points = ["A2", "B3", "C4", "D5", "E6", "F6"]
        light_path = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(path_points)-1):
            line = Line(self.grid[path_points[i]], self.grid[path_points[i+1]], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
            light_path.add(line)
        
        for segment in light_path:
            self.play(Create(segment), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        
        # Snell's Law Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        snell_formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#F0E68C")
        self.place_at_grid(snell_formula, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(snell_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        
        # Transition to Lifeguard path analogy
        self.play(FadeOut(layers), FadeOut(light_path), FadeOut(snell_formula))
        
        # Beach and Water setup
        beach = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#EDC9AF", fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(beach, "A1", "C6")
        water = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#0077BE", fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(water, "D1", "F6")
        
        sand_label = Text("SAND (FAST)", font_size=18, color=BLACK)
        water_label = Text("WATER (SLOW)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(sand_label, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(water_label, "E5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(beach), FadeIn(water), Write(sand_label), Write(water_label))
        
        # Lifeguard optimal path (bending towards the normal when entering water)
        lg_start = self.grid["A1"]
        lg_mid = self.grid["C4"] 
        lg_end = self.grid["F5"]
        
        lg_path = VGroup(
            Line(lg_start, lg_mid, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4),
            Line(lg_mid, lg_end, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        )
        
        self.play(Create(lg_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        
        # Transformation into a smooth optimal curve (Brachistochrone/Cycloid)
        smooth_curve = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        # Defining curve points through grid anchors to keep it smooth
        smooth_curve.set_points_as_corners([self.grid["A1"], self.grid["B2"], self.grid["C4"], self.grid["E5"], self.grid["F6"]])
        smooth_curve.make_smooth()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(beach), FadeOut(water), FadeOut(sand_label), FadeOut(water_label),
            ReplacementTransform(lg_path, smooth_curve)
        )
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Counter-Intuitive Challenge
section_1.content: Introduce the core question: Between two points at different heights, what path allows an object to slide from start to finish in the shortest time? Contrast the 'shortest distance' (straight line) with the 'quickest time'.
section_1.example: An animation of two penguins, Pip and Pop. Pip slides down a straight icy ramp, while Pop slides down a curved ramp. Despite the longer path, Pop reaches the bottom first, sparking the 'Why?'

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Speed and Energy
section_2.content: Review the Conservation of Energy. Establish that speed (v) depends only on the vertical drop (y), represented by the formula v = √(2gy). Explain that while a curve is longer, its steeper start provides higher initial velocity.
section_2.example: A side-view graph showing a marble at various heights. As the height (y) decreases, a velocity vector arrow grows longer, visually linking height loss to speed gain.

section_3.title: The Optical Analogy (Snell's Law)
section_3.content: Introduce Bernoulli's brilliant insight: Treat the falling object like a beam of light passing through layers of varying density. Use Snell's Law (sinθ/v = constant) to explain how light 'chooses' the path of least time.
section_3.example: A visual of a lifeguard on a beach. To reach a drowning swimmer fastest, they don't run in a straight line; they run further on land (where they are fast) and less in water (where they are slow). This 'bending' is the key to the Brachistochrone.

section_4.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
section_4.content: Reveal the Brachistochrone curve as an 'Inverted Cycloid'. Define a cycloid as the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling wheel. Show the parametric relationship where the curve's curvature perfectly balances speed and distance.
section_4.example: An animation of a bicycle wheel rolling along a ceiling. A glowing red dot on the tire's edge traces a graceful arc—this is the exact shape the slide must be.

section_5.title: Properties and Verification
section_5.content: Highlight the 'Tautochrone' property: No matter where you start on the cycloid, you will reach the bottom in the exact same amount of time. Summarize the trade-off between acceleration and path length.
section_5.example: A 'Multi-Ball Race' animation. Three balls are placed at different heights on the same cycloid ramp. They are released simultaneously and all collide at the bottom at the exact same moment.

section_6.title: Real-World Application & Summary
section_6.content: Recap the journey from intuition to the cycloid. Briefly mention applications in engineering, such as the design of efficient roller coasters or gravity-based transit systems.
section_6.example: A montage of modern skatepark bowls and high-speed roller coaster loops, overlaid with the cycloid geometry to show how designers use these principles to maximize thrill and speed.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Counter-Intuitive Challenge"
        lecture_lines = [
            "What path is the fastest between two points?",
            "A straight line is the shortest distance, not time.",
            "Curved paths often allow objects to reach destinations sooner."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_A = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_B = "#00BFFF"
        COLOR_STRAIGHT = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_CURVE = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_FLASH = "#FFFF00"

        # 1. Define Points A and B
        dot_a = Dot(color=COLOR_A)
        dot_b = Dot(color=COLOR_B)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_A)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_B)
        
        self.place_at_grid(dot_a, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_b, "E5")
        label_a.next_to(dot_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_b.next_to(dot_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # 2. Define Paths
        start_pos = self.grid["B2"]
        end_pos = self.grid["E5"]
        
        straight_path = Line(start_pos, end_pos, color=COLOR_STRAIGHT)
        
        # Curve: Cubic Bezier to simulate a faster descent curve (replaces QuadraticBezier)
        # Control point at E2 (drop fast then move right)
        control_pos = self.grid["E2"]
        curved_path = CubicBezier(start_pos, control_pos, control_pos, end_pos, color=COLOR_CURVE)

        # 3. Define Sliders Pip and Pop
        pip = Dot(color=COLOR_STRAIGHT).scale(1.2)
        pip_label = Text("Pip", font_size=18, color=COLOR_STRAIGHT)
        
        pop = Dot(color=COLOR_CURVE).scale(1.2)
        pop_label = Text("Pop", font_size=18, color=COLOR_CURVE)

        # Trackers for movement
        pip_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        pop_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Updaters for position
        pip.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(straight_path.point_from_proportion(pip_tracker.get_value())))
        pip_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(pip, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        pop.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(curved_path.point_from_proportion(pop_tracker.get_value())))
        pop_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(pop, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "What path is the fastest between two points?"
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_a), FadeIn(label_a),
            FadeIn(dot_b), FadeIn(label_b),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "A straight line is the shortest distance, not time."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_STRAIGHT)
        )
        self.play(Create(straight_path), run_time=1)
        self.add(pip, pip_label)
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate.set_value(0.3), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Curved paths often allow objects to reach destinations sooner."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        )
        self.play(Create(curved_path), run_time=1)
        self.add(pop, pop_label)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Race Sequence
        # Reset Pip
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Execution of the race: Pop finishes in 2s, Pip still halfway
        self.play(
            pip_tracker.animate(rate_func=linear).set_value(0.6),
            pop_tracker.animate(rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_quad).set_value(1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Pop reaches B first; curved path flashes yellow
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_FLASH), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_FLASH), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE), run_time=0.2)
        
        # Pip finishes
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate(rate_func=linear).set_value(1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Knowledge: Speed and Energy", [
            "Conservation of energy dictates speed based on vertical drop.",
            "Velocity equals the square root of 2gh.",
            "Steeper starts grant more speed early in the descent."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the energy-to-speed formula v = sqrt(2gy) in white (#FFFFFF)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        formula = MathTex(r"v = \sqrt{2gy}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A3', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a falling marble (#ADFF2F) with its velocity vector (#FF8C00) growing
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#ADFF2F")
        
        start_pt = self.grid['C1']
        end_pt = self.grid['F1']
        
        marble = Dot(point=start_pt, color="#ADFF2F", radius=0.12)
        y_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Arrow function for dynamic updating
        def get_arrow():
            curr_y = y_tracker.get_value()
            curr_pos = start_pt + DOWN * curr_y
            v_len = np.sqrt(curr_y) * 0.8
            if v_len < 0.05:
                return Line(curr_pos, curr_pos, stroke_width=0)
            return Arrow(curr_pos, curr_pos + DOWN * v_len, buff=0, color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4)

        velocity_vector = always_redraw(get_arrow)
        marble.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(start_pt + DOWN * y_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(marble))
        self.add(velocity_vector)
        # Total distance is 3 grid units (C to F)
        self.play(y_tracker.animate.set_value(3), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clear updaters for performance and finalize the state
        frozen_vector = get_arrow()
        marble.clear_updaters()
        self.remove(velocity_vector)
        self.add(frozen_vector)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the steep start of the curve to show rapid speed gain
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlighting Line 3 with yellow
        
        # Cycloid Parametric: x = t - sin(t), y = -(1 - cos(t))
        # This curve starts vertically at t=0
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t - np.sin(t), -(1 - np.cos(t)), 0]),
            t_range=[0, PI],
            color=WHITE
        )
        highlight_segment = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t - np.sin(t), -(1 - np.cos(t)), 0]),
            t_range=[0, PI/4], # The steep initial part
            color="#FFFF00",
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Grouping ensures they share the same transform from place_in_area
        viz_group = VGroup(curve, highlight_segment)
        self.place_in_area(viz_group, 'C3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Draw the curve, then the highlight
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(highlight_segment))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The Optical Analogy (Snell's Law)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Johann Bernoulli used an optical analogy to solve it.",
            "Imagine light traveling through layers with changing refractive indices.",
            "Snell’s Law states sin theta over velocity remains constant.",
            "Light always chooses the path of least time.",
            "This bending light path reveals the optimal physical curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lines
        colors = ["#87CEEB", "#98FB98", "#F0E68C", "#FFA07A", "#DDA0DD"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        
        # Layers of varying density
        # Representing media where light speed changes
        layer_colors = ["#003366", "#004080", "#004d99", "#0059b3", "#0066cc", "#0073e6"]
        layers = VGroup()
        for i in range(6):
            row_char = chr(65 + i)
            rect = Rectangle(width=6.0, height=1.0, fill_color=layer_colors[i], fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0.5, stroke_color=BLUE_E)
            self.place_in_area(rect, f"{row_char}1", f"{row_char}6")
            layers.add(rect)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(layers))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        
        # Bending light path (Piecewise linear segments)
        path_points = ["A2", "B3", "C4", "D5", "E6", "F6"]
        light_path = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(path_points)-1):
            line = Line(self.grid[path_points[i]], self.grid[path_points[i+1]], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
            light_path.add(line)
        
        for segment in light_path:
            self.play(Create(segment), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        
        # Snell's Law Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        snell_formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#F0E68C")
        self.place_at_grid(snell_formula, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(snell_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        
        # Transition to Lifeguard path analogy
        self.play(FadeOut(layers), FadeOut(light_path), FadeOut(snell_formula))
        
        # Beach and Water setup
        beach = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#EDC9AF", fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(beach, "A1", "C6")
        water = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#0077BE", fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(water, "D1", "F6")
        
        sand_label = Text("SAND (FAST)", font_size=18, color=BLACK)
        water_label = Text("WATER (SLOW)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(sand_label, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(water_label, "E5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(beach), FadeIn(water), Write(sand_label), Write(water_label))
        
        # Lifeguard optimal path (bending towards the normal when entering water)
        lg_start = self.grid["A1"]
        lg_mid = self.grid["C4"] 
        lg_end = self.grid["F5"]
        
        lg_path = VGroup(
            Line(lg_start, lg_mid, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4),
            Line(lg_mid, lg_end, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        )
        
        self.play(Create(lg_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        
        # Transformation into a smooth optimal curve (Brachistochrone/Cycloid)
        smooth_curve = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        # Defining curve points through grid anchors to keep it smooth
        smooth_curve.set_points_as_corners([self.grid["A1"], self.grid["B2"], self.grid["C4"], self.grid["E5"], self.grid["F6"]])
        smooth_curve.make_smooth()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(beach), FadeOut(water), FadeOut(sand_label), FadeOut(water_label),
            ReplacementTransform(lg_path, smooth_curve)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Solution: The Cycloid"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The fastest path is an inverted cycloid curve.",
            "A cycloid is traced by a point on a rolling wheel.",
            "Its parametric equations balance path length and acceleration.",
            "Gravity accelerates the object most efficiently along this arc.",
            "This curve is the unique solution to the Brachistochrone problem."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # A wheel (#D3D3D3) appears and rolls along a flat ceiling line.
        ceiling_start = self.grid["A1"]
        ceiling_end = self.grid["A6"]
        ceiling = Line(ceiling_start, ceiling_end, color=WHITE)
        
        radius = 0.4
        wheel_start_center = [self.grid["A1"][0] + 0.5, self.grid["A1"][1] - radius, 0]
        wheel_circ = Circle(radius=radius, color="#D3D3D3")
        wheel_circ.move_to(wheel_start_center)
        spoke = Line(wheel_circ.get_center(), wheel_circ.get_top(), color="#D3D3D3")
        wheel_group = VGroup(wheel_circ, spoke)
        
        self.play(Create(ceiling), FadeIn(wheel_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # A red dot (#FF0000) on the rim traces an arc as the wheel rolls.
        dot = Dot(radius=0.08, color="#FF0000")
        dot.move_to(wheel_circ.get_top())
        
        theta_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_wheel_motion(obj):
            t = theta_tracker.get_value()
            cx = wheel_start_center[0] + radius * t
            cy = wheel_start_center[1]
            obj[0].move_to([cx, cy, 0])
            obj[1].put_start_and_end_on(
                [cx, cy, 0],
                [cx + radius * np.sin(t), cy + radius * np.cos(t), 0]
            )

        def update_dot_motion(obj):
            t = theta_tracker.get_value()
            cx = wheel_start_center[0] + radius * t
            cy = wheel_start_center[1]
            # Point starts at contact (top) at t=0
            obj.move_to([cx + radius * np.sin(t), cy + radius * np.cos(t), 0])

        wheel_group.add_updater(update_wheel_motion)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot_motion)
        
        # Tracing the path in vibrant light blue (#00FFFF)
        trace = TracedPath(dot.get_center, stroke_color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        
        self.add(dot, trace)
        # Roll across (one full rotation)
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(TAU), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # The full cycloid path is drawn in a vibrant light blue (#00FFFF).
        # Create a static ParametricFunction to replace the trace
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([
                wheel_start_center[0] + radius * t + radius * np.sin(t),
                wheel_start_center[1] + radius * np.cos(t),
                0
            ]),
            t_range=[0, TAU],
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        
        # Remove dynamic elements
        wheel_group.remove_updater(update_wheel_motion)
        dot.remove_updater(update_dot_motion)
        self.remove(trace, dot)
        self.add(cycloid_path)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(wheel_group), FadeOut(ceiling))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # The curve is inverted to match the sliding path between points.
        # Shift to center area and scale up for emphasis
        slide_version = cycloid_path.copy()
        self.place_in_area(slide_version, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=1.6)
        
        self.play(Transform(cycloid_path, slide_version))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # The label 'Cycloid' (#FFD700) appears next to the final shape.
        label = Text("Cycloid", color="#FFD700", font_size=36)
        label.next_to(cycloid_path, UP, buff=0.4)
        
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Lecture lines for Section 5
        lines = [
            "The cycloid also possesses the remarkable Tautochrone property.",
            "Objects released from any height reach the bottom simultaneously.",
            "Higher starting points cover more distance but move faster.",
            "These factors perfectly cancel out to keep time constant.",
            "This consistency confirms the cycloid's mathematical perfection."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Properties and Verification", lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid point calculation
        # x = r(theta + sin(theta)), y = r(1 - cos(theta))
        # theta in [-PI, 0] for a slide starting high on left and ending low at 0
        r_val = 0.7
        def get_cycloid_point(theta):
            return np.array([r_val * (theta + np.sin(theta)), r_val * (1 - np.cos(theta)), 0])

        # Create Ramp
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(
            get_cycloid_point,
            t_range=[-PI, 0],
            color="#C0C0C0"
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_path, "B1", "F6")
        self.play(Create(cycloid_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Define starting thetas for three balls
        thetas_start = [-0.9 * PI, -0.6 * PI, -0.3 * PI]
        colors = ["#FF00FF", "#00FF00", "#00FFFF"]
        balls = VGroup()
        for col in colors:
            ball = Dot(radius=0.1, color=col)
            balls.add(ball)

        # Initial positioning of balls
        for i, theta in enumerate(thetas_start):
            balls[i].move_to(cycloid_path.point_from_proportion((theta + PI) / PI))

        self.play(FadeIn(balls))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Time tracker for the harmonic motion
        # Theta(t) = Theta_0 * cos(PI/2 * t_norm)
        # We'll normalize t so that at t=1, all reach theta=0.
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        def update_ball(ball, theta_0):
            t_curr = time_tracker.get_value()
            current_theta = theta_0 * np.cos((PI / 2) * t_curr)
            # Map theta to proportion [0, 1] on the path [-PI, 0]
            prop = (current_theta + PI) / PI
            ball.move_to(cycloid_path.point_from_proportion(prop))

        # Add updaters
        for i in range(len(balls)):
            balls[i].add_updater(lambda b, idx=i: update_ball(b, thetas_start[idx]))

        # Start motion
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Balls are all at the bottom now. Add a small highlight or flash
        arrival_flash = Flash(cycloid_path.get_end(), color=WHITE, flash_radius=0.5)
        self.play(arrival_flash)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Clear updaters for static end
        for b in balls:
            b.clear_updaters()
            
        self.wait(3)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Real-World Application & Summary",
            [
                "From physics puzzles to modern engineering and roller coasters.",
                "The cycloid principles optimize speed and passenger thrill.",
                "Calculus of variations proves the beauty of the quickest descent."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visual comparison of the straight line vs. the optimal cycloid descent.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        start_pt = self.grid["B1"]
        end_pt = self.grid["E5"]
        
        # Straight path
        straight_path = Line(start_pt, end_pt, color=BLUE_B)
        
        # Cycloid-like path (Steep start, transitioning to horizontal)
        cycloid_path = CubicBezier(
            start_pt, 
            start_pt + 3 * DOWN, 
            end_pt + 1.5 * LEFT, 
            end_pt, 
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        # Racing dots
        ball_straight = Dot(color=BLUE_B)
        ball_cycloid = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        
        # Labels
        label_s = Text("Straight Line", font_size=16, color=BLUE_B)
        label_c = Text("Optimal Cycloid", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(label_s, "A4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "A2", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            Create(straight_path),
            Create(cycloid_path),
            Write(label_s),
            Write(label_c)
        )
        
        # The race animation
        # The cycloid path dot finishes significantly faster
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(ball_cycloid, cycloid_path, rate_func=linear, run_time=1.8),
            MoveAlongPath(ball_straight, straight_path, rate_func=linear, run_time=2.6)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Cleanup for next segment
        self.play(
            FadeOut(straight_path),
            FadeOut(ball_straight),
            FadeOut(ball_cycloid),
            FadeOut(label_s),
            FadeOut(label_c),
            cycloid_path.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.2)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Overlay a cycloid curve (#FFFF00) onto a skatepark bowl silhouette.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Bowl silhouette using a rounded rectangle/arc
        bowl_silhouette = Arc(radius=2.2, start_angle=PI, angle=PI, color=GREY_D, stroke_width=12)
        self.place_in_area(bowl_silhouette, "C1", "F6")
        
        # Matching cycloid curve to overlay
        cycloid_overlay = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([2 * (t - np.sin(t)), -2 * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0]),
            t_range=[0.5, TAU-0.5], # Show a significant portion
            color=YELLOW
        ).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_overlay, "C1", "F6")

        self.play(Create(bowl_silhouette))
        self.play(Create(cycloid_overlay))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(bowl_silhouette),
            FadeOut(cycloid_overlay),
            FadeOut(cycloid_path)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The text 'The Path of Quickest Descent' fades in (#FFFFFF).
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        final_summary = Text("The Path of Quickest Descent", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(final_summary, "B1", "E6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(final_summary))
        self.wait(4)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Real-World Application & Summary",
            [
                "From physics puzzles to modern engineering and roller coasters.",
                "The cycloid principles optimize speed and passenger thrill.",
                "Calculus of variations proves the beauty of the quickest descent."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visual comparison of the straight line vs. the optimal cycloid descent.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        start_pt = self.grid["B1"]
        end_pt = self.grid["E5"]
        
        # Straight path
        straight_path = Line(start_pt, end_pt, color=BLUE_B)
        
        # Cycloid-like path (Steep start, transitioning to horizontal)
        cycloid_path = CubicBezier(
            start_pt, 
            start_pt + 3 * DOWN, 
            end_pt + 1.5 * LEFT, 
            end_pt, 
            color=YELLOW
        )
        
        # Racing dots
        ball_straight = Dot(color=BLUE_B)
        ball_cycloid = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        
        # Labels
        label_s = Text("Straight Line", font_size=16, color=BLUE_B)
        label_c = Text("Optimal Cycloid", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(label_s, "A4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "A2", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            Create(straight_path),
            Create(cycloid_path),
            Write(label_s),
            Write(label_c)
        )
        
        # The race animation
        # The cycloid path dot finishes significantly faster
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(ball_cycloid, cycloid_path, rate_func=linear, run_time=1.8),
            MoveAlongPath(ball_straight, straight_path, rate_func=linear, run_time=2.6)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Cleanup for next segment
        self.play(
            FadeOut(straight_path),
            FadeOut(ball_straight),
            FadeOut(ball_cycloid),
            FadeOut(label_s),
            FadeOut(label_c),
            cycloid_path.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.2)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Overlay a cycloid curve (#FFFF00) onto a skatepark bowl silhouette.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Bowl silhouette using a rounded rectangle/arc
        bowl_silhouette = Arc(radius=2.2, start_angle=PI, angle=PI, color=GREY_D, stroke_width=12)
        self.place_in_area(bowl_silhouette, "C1", "F6")
        
        # Matching cycloid curve to overlay
        cycloid_overlay = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([2 * (t - np.sin(t)), -2 * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0]),
            t_range=[0.5, TAU-0.5], # Show a significant portion
            color=YELLOW
        ).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_overlay, "C1", "F6")

        self.play(Create(bowl_silhouette))
        self.play(Create(cycloid_overlay))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(bowl_silhouette),
            FadeOut(cycloid_overlay),
            FadeOut(cycloid_path)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The text 'The Path of Quickest Descent' fades in (#FFFFFF).
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        final_summary = Text("The Path of Quickest Descent", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(final_summary, "B1", "E6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(final_summary))
        self.wait(4)

            cx = wheel_start_center[0] + radius * t
            cy = wheel_start_center[1]
            obj[0].move_to([cx, cy, 0])
            obj[1].put_start_and_end_on(
                [cx, cy, 0],
                [cx + radius * np.sin(t), cy + radius * np.cos(t), 0]
            )

        def update_dot_motion(obj):
            t = theta_tracker.get_value()
            cx = wheel_start_center[0] + radius * t
            cy = wheel_start_center[1]
            # Point starts at contact (top) at t=0
            obj.move_to([cx + radius * np.sin(t), cy + radius * np.cos(t), 0])

        wheel_group.add_updater(update_wheel_motion)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot_motion)
        
        # Tracing the path in vibrant light blue (#00FFFF)
        trace = TracedPath(dot.get_center, stroke_color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        
        self.add(dot, trace)
        # Roll across (one full rotation)
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(TAU), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # The full cycloid path is drawn in a vibrant light blue (#00FFFF).
        # Create a static ParametricFunction to replace the trace
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([
                wheel_start_center[0] + radius * t + radius * np.sin(t),
                wheel_start_center[1] + radius * np.cos(t),
                0
            ]),
            t_range=[0, TAU],
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        
        # Remove dynamic elements
        wheel_group.remove_updater(update_wheel_motion)
        dot.remove_updater(update_dot_motion)
        self.remove(trace, dot)
        self.add(cycloid_path)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(wheel_group), FadeOut(ceiling))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):

        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Knowledge: Speed and Energy", [
            "Conservation of energy dictates speed based on vertical drop.",
            "Velocity equals the square root of 2gh.",
            "Steeper starts grant more speed early in the descent."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the energy-to-speed formula v = sqrt(2gy) in white (#FFFFFF)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        formula = MathTex(r"v = \sqrt{2gy}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A3', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a falling marble (#ADFF2F) with its velocity vector (#FF8C00) growing
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#ADFF2F")
        
        start_pt = self.grid['C1']
        end_pt = self.grid['F1']
        
        marble = Dot(point=start_pt, color="#ADFF2F", radius=0.12)
        y_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Arrow function for dynamic updating
        def get_arrow():
            curr_y = y_tracker.get_value()
            curr_pos = start_pt + DOWN * curr_y
            v_len = np.sqrt(curr_y) * 0.8
            if v_len < 0.05:
                return Line(curr_pos, curr_pos, stroke_width=0)
            return Arrow(curr_pos, curr_pos + DOWN * v_len, buff=0, color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4)

        velocity_vector = always_redraw(get_arrow)
        marble.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(start_pt + DOWN * y_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(marble))
        self.add(velocity_vector)
        # Total distance is 3 grid units (C to F)
        self.play(y_tracker.animate.set_value(3), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clear updaters for performance and finalize the state
        frozen_vector = get_arrow()
        marble.clear_updaters()
        self.remove(velocity_vector)
        self.add(frozen_vector)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlighting Line 3 with yellow
        
        # Cycloid Parametric: x = t - sin(t), y = -(1 - cos(t))
        # This curve starts vertically at t=0
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t - np.sin(t), -(1 - np.cos(t)), 0]),
            t_range=[0, PI],
            color=WHITE
        )
        highlight_segment = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t - np.sin(t), -(1 - np.cos(t)), 0]),
            t_range=[0, PI/4], # The steep initial part
            color="#FFFF00",
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Grouping ensures they share the same transform from place_in_area
        viz_group = VGroup(curve, highlight_segment)
        self.place_in_area(viz_group, 'C3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Draw the curve, then the highlight
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(highlight_segment))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Lecture lines for Section 5
        lines = [
            "The cycloid also possesses the remarkable Tautochrone property.",
            "Objects released from any height reach the bottom simultaneously.",
            "Higher starting points cover more distance but move faster.",
            "These factors perfectly cancel out to keep time constant.",
            "This consistency confirms the cycloid's mathematical perfection."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Properties and Verification", lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid point calculation
        # x = r(theta + sin(theta)), y = r(1 - cos(theta))
        # theta in [-PI, 0] for a slide starting high on left and ending low at 0
        r_val = 0.7
        def get_cycloid_point(theta):
            return np.array([r_val * (theta + np.sin(theta)), r_val * (1 - np.cos(theta)), 0])

        # Create Ramp
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(
            get_cycloid_point,
            t_range=[-PI, 0],
            color="#C0C0C0"
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_path, "B1", "F6")
        self.play(Create(cycloid_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Define starting thetas for three balls
        thetas_start = [-0.9 * PI, -0.6 * PI, -0.3 * PI]
        colors = ["#FF00FF", "#00FF00", "#00FFFF"]
        balls = VGroup()
        for col in colors:
            ball = Dot(radius=0.1, color=col)
            balls.add(ball)

        # Initial positioning of balls
        for i, theta in enumerate(thetas_start):
            balls[i].move_to(cycloid_path.point_from_proportion((theta + PI) / PI))

        self.play(FadeIn(balls))
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Time tracker for the harmonic motion
        # Theta(t) = Theta_0 * cos(PI/2 * t_norm)
        # We'll normalize t so that at t=1, all reach theta=0.
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        def update_ball(ball, theta_0):
            t_curr = time_tracker.get_value()
            current_theta = theta_0 * np.cos((PI / 2) * t_curr)
            # Map theta to proportion [0, 1] on the path [-PI, 0]
            prop = (current_theta + PI) / PI
            ball.move_to(cycloid_path.point_from_proportion(prop))

        # Add updaters
        for i in range(len(balls)):
            balls[i].add_updater(lambda b, idx=i: update_ball(b, thetas_start[idx]))

        # Start motion
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Balls are all at the bottom now. Add a small highlight or flash
        arrival_flash = Flash(cycloid_path.get_end(), color=WHITE, flash_radius=0.5)
        self.play(arrival_flash)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Clear updaters for static end
        for b in balls:
            b.clear_updaters()
            
        self.wait(3)

        pip_label = Text("Pip", font_size=18, color=COLOR_STRAIGHT)

        pop_label = Text("Pop", font_size=18, color=COLOR_CURVE)

        # Trackers for movement
        pip_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        pop_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Updaters for position
        pip.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(straight_path.point_from_proportion(pip_tracker.get_value())))
        pip_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(pip, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        pop.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(curved_path.point_from_proportion(pop_tracker.get_value())))
        pop_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(pop, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "What path is the fastest between two points?"
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_a), FadeIn(label_a),
            FadeIn(dot_b), FadeIn(label_b),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "A straight line is the shortest distance, not time."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_STRAIGHT)
        )
        self.play(Create(straight_path), run_time=1)
        self.add(pip, pip_label)
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate.set_value(0.3), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Curved paths often allow objects to reach destinations sooner."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        )
        self.play(Create(curved_path), run_time=1)
        self.add(pop, pop_label)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Race Sequence
        # Reset Pip
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Execution of the race: Pop finishes in 2s, Pip still halfway
        self.play(
            pip_tracker.animate(rate_func=linear).set_value(0.6),
            pop_tracker.animate(rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_quad).set_value(1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Pop reaches B first; curved path flashes yellow
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_FLASH), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_FLASH), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(curved_path.animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE), run_time=0.2)
        
        # Pip finishes
        self.play(pip_tracker.animate(rate_func=linear).set_value(1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Optical Analogy (Snell's Law)
outline.content: Introduce Bernoulli's brilliant insight: Treat the falling object like a beam of light passing through layers of varying density. Use Snell's Law (sinθ/v = constant) to explain how light 'chooses' the path of least time.
outline.example: A visual of a lifeguard on a beach. To reach a drowning swimmer fastest, they don't run in a straight line; they run further on land (where they are fast) and less in water (where they are slow). This 'bending' is the key to the Brachistochrone.

storyboard.title: The Optical Analogy (Snell's Law)
lecture_lines: Johann Bernoulli used an optical analogy to solve it.
Imagine light traveling through layers with changing refractive indices.
Snell’s Law states sin theta over velocity remains constant.
Light always chooses the path of least time.
This bending light path reveals the optimal physical curve.
animations: Show horizontal layers with varying colors (#1A1A1A to #4D4D4D).
Light beam (#FFFF00) enters and bends at each interface.
Display Snell's Law: sin(theta)/v = constant in yellow (#F0E68C).
Lifeguard path (#FF4500) bends at beach-water transition point.
Light path morphs into smooth Brachistochrone curve (#00FFFF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The Optical Analogy (Snell's Law)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Johann Bernoulli used an optical analogy to solve it.",
            "Imagine light traveling through layers with changing refractive indices.",
            "Snell’s Law states sin theta over velocity remains constant.",
            "Light always chooses the path of least time.",
            "This bending light path reveals the optimal physical curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lines
        colors = ["#87CEEB", "#98FB98", "#F0E68C", "#FFA07A", "#DDA0DD"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        
        # Layers of varying density
        # Representing media where light speed changes
        layer_colors = ["#003366", "#004080", "#004d99", "#0059b3", "#0066cc", "#0073e6"]
        layers = VGroup()
        for i in range(6):
            row_char = chr(65 + i)
            rect = Rectangle(width=6.0, height=1.0, fill_color=layer_colors[i], fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0.5, stroke_color=BLUE_E)
            self.place_in_area(rect, f"{row_char}1", f"{row_char}6")
            layers.add(rect)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(layers))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        
        # Bending light path (Piecewise linear segments)
        path_points = ["A2", "B3", "C4", "D5", "E6", "F6"]
        light_path = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(path_points)-1):
            line = Line(self.grid[path_points[i]], self.grid[path_points[i+1]], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
            light_path.add(line)
        
        for segment in light_path:
            self.play(Create(segment), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        
        # Snell's Law Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        snell_formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#F0E68C")
        self.place_at_grid(snell_formula, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(snell_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        
        # Transition to Lifeguard path analogy
        self.play(FadeOut(layers), FadeOut(light_path), FadeOut(snell_formula))
        
        # Beach and Water setup
        beach = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#EDC9AF", fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(beach, "A1", "C6")

        self.place_in_area(water, "D1", "F6")
        
        sand_label = Text("SAND (FAST)", font_size=18, color=BLACK)
        water_label = Text("WATER (SLOW)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(sand_label, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(water_label, "E5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(beach), FadeIn(water), Write(sand_label), Write(water_label))
        
        # Lifeguard optimal path (bending towards the normal when entering water)
        lg_start = self.grid["A1"]
        lg_mid = self.grid["C4"] 
        lg_end = self.grid["F5"]
        
        lg_path = VGroup(
            Line(lg_start, lg_mid, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4),
            Line(lg_mid, lg_end, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        )
        
        self.play(Create(lg_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        
        # Transformation into a smooth optimal curve (Brachistochrone/Cycloid)
        smooth_curve = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        # Defining curve points through grid anchors to keep it smooth
        smooth_curve.set_points_as_corners([self.grid["A1"], self.grid["B2"], self.grid["C4"], self.grid["E5"], self.grid["F6"]])
        smooth_curve.make_smooth()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(beach), FadeOut(water), FadeOut(sand_label), FadeOut(water_label),
            ReplacementTransform(lg_path, smooth_curve)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Knowledge: Speed and Energy", [
            "Conservation of energy dictates speed based on vertical drop.",
            "Velocity equals the square root of 2gh.",
            "Steeper starts grant more speed early in the descent."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the energy-to-speed formula v = sqrt(2gy) in white (#FFFFFF)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        formula = MathTex(r"v = \sqrt{2gy}", color=WHITE)
        # Issue 29: Fixed scale and position
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A4', 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a falling marble [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marble.svg]
        # with its velocity vector (#FF8C00) growing.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#ADFF2F") # Matching marble color (approx)
        
        start_pt = self.grid['C1']
        
        # Issue 25: Integrate SVG asset
        marble = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/marble.svg")
        marble.set_color("#ADFF2F")
        self.place_at_grid(marble, 'C1', scale_factor=0.3)
        
        y_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Create vector. Update its points to avoid redraw overhead.
        velocity_vector = Arrow(start_pt, start_pt, buff=0, color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4)

        lecture_lines = [
            "Johann Bernoulli used an optical analogy to solve it.",
            "Imagine light traveling through layers with changing refractive indices.",
            "Snell’s Law states sin theta over velocity remains constant.",
            "Light always chooses the path of least time.",
            "This bending light path reveals the optimal physical curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lines
        colors = ["#87CEEB", "#98FB98", "#F0E68C", "#FFA07A", "#DDA0DD"]

        layer_colors = ["#1A1A1A", "#242424", "#2E2E2E", "#383838", "#424242", "#4D4D4D"]

            light_path.add(line)

        self.wait(1)

        self.play(Write(snell_formula))

        water = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#0077BE", fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(water, "D1", "F6")
        
        sand_label = Text("SAND (FAST)", font_size=18, color=BLACK)
        water_label = Text("WATER (SLOW)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        
        # Issue 32 & 33 Fixes: sand_label at 'C6', water_label at 'F6'
        self.place_at_grid(sand_label, 'C6')
        self.place_at_grid(water_label, 'F6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(beach), FadeIn(water), Write(sand_label), Write(water_label))
        
        # Lifeguard optimal path (bending towards the normal when entering water)
        # Lifeguard path (#FF4500)
        lg_start = self.grid["A1"]
        lg_mid = self.grid["C4"] 
        lg_end = self.grid["F5"]
        
        lg_path = VGroup(
            Line(lg_start, lg_mid, color="#FF4500", stroke_width=4),
            Line(lg_mid, lg_end, color="#FF4500", stroke_width=4)
        )
        
        self.play(Create(lg_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        
        # Transformation into a smooth optimal curve (Brachistochrone/Cycloid)
        # Smooth Brachistochrone curve (#00FFFF)
        smooth_curve = VMobject(color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=6)
        # Defining curve points through grid anchors to keep it smooth
        smooth_curve.set_points_as_corners([self.grid["A1"], self.grid["B2"], self.grid["C4"], self.grid["E5"], self.grid["F6"]])

        self.play(
            FadeOut(beach), FadeOut(water), FadeOut(sand_label), FadeOut(water_label),
            ReplacementTransform(lg_path, smooth_curve)
        )

        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Lecture lines for Section 5
        lines = [
            "The cycloid also possesses the remarkable Tautochrone property.",
            "Objects released from any height reach the bottom simultaneously.",
            "Higher starting points cover more distance but move faster.",
            "These factors perfectly cancel out to keep time constant.",
            "This consistency confirms the cycloid's mathematical perfection."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Properties and Verification", lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid point calculation
        # x = r(theta + sin(theta)), y = r(1 - cos(theta))
        # theta in [-PI, 0] for a slide starting high on left and ending low at 0
        r_val = 0.7
        def get_cycloid_point(theta):
            return np.array([r_val * (theta + np.sin(theta)), r_val * (1 - np.cos(theta)), 0])

        # Create Ramp
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(
            get_cycloid_point,
            t_range=[-PI, 0],
            color="#C0C0C0"
        )
